memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: In the fourteenth year, Kedorlaomer and the kings allied with him went out and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh Kiriathaim and the Horites in the hill country of Seir... Then they turned back and went to En Mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and they conquered the whole territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites... - Gen 14:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Kedorlaomer's army rolls through the region, crushing everything in its path - Rephaites, Zuzites, Emites, Horites, Amalekites, Amorites. People after people, defeated and swept aside. Whole nations reduced to a single line in a list of conquests. This is what the machinery of war looks like from a distance: names on a page.

But every one of those names was a people. Families, children, homes, lives. Behind the tidy summary of conquest lies immense human suffering. Scripture records it plainly, without glorifying it. War is not adventure; it is loss upon loss.

It is worth letting this sober us. Our world still runs on this logic - the strong sweeping over the weak, whole populations displaced and destroyed, reduced in the retelling to statistics. God sees what the history books flatten. Every one of those forgotten peoples was made in His image.

And this is why the world needs a different kind of King. The kings of Genesis 14 conquer by crushing; Christ conquers by being crushed. He is the King who came "not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many" (Matt 20:28). One day He will end all wars, and "nation will not take up sword against nation" (Isa 2:4). Until then, we grieve what war costs and long for the King who brings peace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see the human cost behind the world's conflicts, or just the headlines?
- How does Christ's way of conquering differ from the world's?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You see every person behind the headlines of war and loss. Give me Your heart for the suffering, and hasten the day when Christ ends all conflict and brings lasting peace.
Amen.
